facts.fact: Based in Cape Town, South Africa (site footer: 'Cape Town, South Africa'; homepage: 'Designed and made locally').
Founding story: started because the founders couldn't find a local golf brand that spoke to them; they loved the game but found its culture stiff, narrow and exclusionary.

The name refers to the small personal habits people fall into when focus matters: the club waggle before a shot, stepping back to check alignment, the breath before committing. The brand extends it beyond golf (a tennis player's ball bounces, a footballer's run-up, a morning coffee routine).
Tagline: 'a modern expression of heritage'; brand mark/initials ORGC (Odd Ritual Golf Club).
Three brand pillars on the shop page: Community (number one rule is 'be lekker'), Creativity, and Craft.
Products are locally made in Cape Town (stated on product pages, e.g. Pleated Daily Trouser and Minimal Wordmark Tee).

Range currently branded 'Collection 01 & 02' on the shop: polos (Classic, Motus, 1990s Heritage), tees, Pleated Daily Trouser, Caddie Jacket, Traditions crewneck, many caps (Script, Script Dad, Heritage Rope, Versa Nylon Crush, Horizon Utility), crew socks. Prices run roughly R 100 to R 1,900 on sale today.
Signature/featured pieces on the homepage: The Caddie Jacket [Navy], ORGC Traditions Crewneck [Burgundy], 1990s Heritage Polo, Pleated Daily Trouser.
Collab: PGG X ODD tees and corduroy caps.
Giving back / community partners listed on homepage: Fairways to Africa, StartWell Foundation, 242 (coffee), Running Late Club.
Ships within South Africa only by default (via Bob Go); international orders by custom arrangement over email.
Founder names: NOT published on the About page, homepage, shop page or shipping policy checked today. Do not name founders.

quotes.quote: We started Odd Ritual because we couldn't find a golf brand locally that spoke to us.
Everyone has their own weird little process. Their own weird routine they go through, their odd ritual.
A brand for people who love the game but want to feel like themselves on the course. Less rigid, more real.
We're not trying to tear anything down — we're just here to open the door a little wider.
at Odd Ritual our number one Rule is 'be lekker'.
